rationale: While MedGen documentation of Rots et al. records downslanted palpebral fissures and epicanthus as features of the KDM6B-related neurodevelopmental disorder (Stolerman syndrome), chromatin modifier reviews such as Rezazadeh et al. (2025) note long palpebral fissures in the context of chromatinopathy differential phenotypes including KDM6B. Furthermore, the provided source excerpts do not contain the complete granular numerators and denominators from the Rots et al. cohort to verify the strict 10% to 25% frequency range or to definitively exclude all occurrences of palpebral fissure elongation across all 72 individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence and quantitative measurement of palpebral fissure length (HP:0000587 vs HP:0000508) in the supplementary phenotypic database of Rots et al. (2023)?
new_directions.rationale: Direct evaluation of the 72-patient supplemental clinical matrix from Rots et al. is required to resolve whether true palpebral fissure elongation was explicitly screened, measured via z-scores, or observed in any subcohort.

new_directions.question_text: How reliably does the facial gestalt distinguish KDM6B-related syndrome from Kabuki syndrome (KMT2D/KDM6A) using automated facial dysmorphology analysis (e.g., DeepGestalt/Face2Gene)?
new_directions.rationale: Because both conditions involve histone demethylase/methyltransferase machinery and share periorbital and distal skeletal findings, objective computer-vision dysmorphology analysis would clarify the discriminative power of fissure shape versus length.
